title: Arbitrary finite rectangular axis-parity matching theorem
question: For any finite rectangular integer box with all side lengths at least two, does the axis plus lower-endpoint parity colouring partition nearest-neighbour edges into two matching layers per axis, with the exact edge-count formula?

finite_contract.box_family: all ordered side triples in [side_min, side_max]^dimension
finite_contract.adjacency: one-coordinate increment by one inside the box

derived_rule.matching_condition: each vertex has at most one incident edge in each layer
derived_rule.parity_separation: the forward and backward candidate lower coordinates differ by one and cannot share parity mod 2

assumptions: Vertices are integer coordinate vectors in a finite rectangular box with every side length at least two.
Edges are only nearest-neighbour coordinate increments and have a unique lower endpoint and axis.
The layer colour is the axis together with the lower endpoint coordinate modulo two; empty colour slots remain represented.
The Lean theorem quantifies over arbitrary finite dimension and side functions for the local matching implication, while the executable aggregate sweep is three-dimensional.
The finite [2,8]^3 sweep is an implementation cross-check of the general combinatorial theorem, not an operator or thermodynamic limit.
missing_assumptions: A weighted Q3LOCK interaction/operator theorem transferring the arbitrary-box layers to a common representation and domain.
Representation-independent common cores, product-domain estimates and onsite self-adjointness for the layer subflows.
Cutoff-, source-, phase-, volume- and exhaustion-uniform boundary commutator and history-tail estimates.
All-shape exhaustion Cauchy, Lie--Trotter/common-alpha convergence and Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification.
Sector coercivity, phase selection, physical-empty comparison, continuum passage and any Yang--Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
stop_conditions: If any declared side triple has a side below two, fail the contract.
If an edge-count formula or retained layer key disagrees, fail the sweep.
If any layer has two incident edges at one vertex, fail the matching audit.
If the independent reconstruction disagrees with the primary aggregate, retain the disagreement and do not average it away.
Do not promote the arbitrary-box combinatorial theorem to a weighted operator, physical, Yang--Mills or mass-gap theorem.
evidence_level: T0 / GENERAL FINITE-COMBINATORIAL THEOREM WITH LEAN LOCAL-INCIDENCE PROOF AND EXECUTED [2,8]^3 CROSS-CHECK
non_claims: No Q3LOCK Hamiltonian, weighted split form, Friedrichs domain or common-core theorem.
No boundary commutator, history-tail, common-alpha or exhaustion theorem.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, sector coercivity, physical-empty comparison, continuum limit or Sector-A/Pre-A closure.
No Yang-Mills dynamics or mass-gap conclusion.

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean proves the arbitrary finite local incidence implication and six-colour arithmetic; Python checks exact edge counts and matching aggregates for the declared [2,8]^3 family.

boundary: R-443 closes only the abstract arbitrary finite-box axis-parity matching property and exact edge-count bookkeeping, with the local incidence implication proved in Lean. It does not close weighted Q3LOCK forms, operator domains, boundary/history tails, exhaustion, common alpha, KMS/GNS, physical-empty, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap claims.
